newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish govt against Universal /Hyundai jv.
newsitem.headline: Polish govt against Universal /Hyundai jv.

text.p: Poland's industry ministry said on Wednesday it was against awarding a car assembly licence to a joint venture beween trading firm Universal SA and South Korea's Hyundai.
Ministry spokeswoman Beata Nawracka said it would recommend denying the licence to the venture.
"According to our experts Universal should not get the licence because the plant it owns does not fulfil requirements of an assembly centre," she told Reuters.
The foreign trade ministry, which awards the licences, has not yet decided on whether to grant one to Universal, the ministry's spokesman Zbigniew Ostrowski said.
The Polish government imposed the licences last month to curb assembly by companies planning to take advantage of Poland's booming car market without larger investment.
The licence allows a car company to import auto parts free of duty, which amounts to between six percent and 35 percent.
Under the old regulations, any firm assembling more than 1,000 cars annually was automatically exempted from the duty.
Universal, which wanted to assemble 15,000 of Hyundai's Accent models, said it still hoped for the licence.
"We fulfil all requirements and we don't see any legal reasons why we shouldn't get the permission," Universal spokesman Krzysztof Bien said.

Universal plans to launch Hyundai cars assembly caused serious concern to South Korea's Daewoo Corp, which bought two car factories in Poland last year and plans to invest about $1.5 billion there in the next six years.
Government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said Daewoo had sent a letter to Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz protesting against the Hyundai assembly plant plans.
Newspapers earlier said that in the letter, Daewoo threatened to trim or abandon its investment plans in Poland if the government allowed such ventures as that of Hyundai and Universal.
